column1: Shared memory (one memory connecting the four intelligences)
column2: 'One shared understanding across your stack' + 'Sybill captures context wherever it lives and puts that understanding to work wherever your team works.' FAQ: 'Sybill is built on different infrastructure: identity, context, memory, learning.' (https://www.sybill.ai/)
column3: 'Encode everything your team knows about winning.' Twin 'Encodes' rep knowledge; 'When a rep transitions off an account, the knowledge usually goes with them. Not anymore. The twin holds that memory permanently, carrying forward all the context you need.' (https://www.getaida.com/, https://www.getaida.com/platform)
column4: 'The world's richest revenue graph, a team of specialized AI agents, and apps your team loves to use. All designed to help your revenue team win.' (aria-label of the letter-spaced homepage subheading, https://www.gong.io/); Revenue Graph product card on homepage
column5: Promise: 'Know every deal. Coach every rep. Forget nothing.'; one memory in three layers. Layer 1 ('What was said') is backed by Built call capture (calendar sync, transcripts, call summaries) and documents (Content Library); its email and Slack sources are In build / Planned. In build: 'Memory layers two and three: what calls meant, and what happened next'. Flagged by the Narrative: 'Connecting the dots (the pricing example)'.
column6: Overlap: all three claim cross-source context on the inspected pages. Difference: Gong's graph is data-graph framing; Aida's twin is per-rep knowledge encoding; Sybill uses 'shared understanding' and memory-infrastructure language ('identity, context, memory, learning') but places it below the hero. Testing hypothesis: an explicit memory-first hero position is not occupied by any of these three pages on the inspection date. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): The memory-first hero remains unoccupied on these pages, but PitchSense's memory layers 2–3 are In build, so a memory-first hero would rest on unbuilt items (Phase 3, Table D hypothesis 1).

column1: Cross-channel intelligence (calls, CRM, emails, Slack, documents)
column2: 'Sybill records calls, meetings, emails, and Slack threads' + '3,000+ other tools' (https://www.sybill.ai/)
column3: 'The full stack your reps actually use. Every day.': Call recording & sales intelligence, AI meeting prep briefs, Personalized email drafting, CRM auto-update, Commitment & promise tracking; 'Aida does the reasoning and stores the result. Every call updates the deal picture: the risks, the commitments, the stakeholder map. It's not reading transcripts. It's working from the compounded intelligence of every conversation since day one.' (https://www.getaida.com/platform)
column4: 'Capture every interaction' (hero, https://www.gong.io/); multimodal revenue signal processing (meta description, https://www.gong.io/)
column5: Built: transcripts from Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Fireflies, Fathom and Granola; summaries and pre-call brief delivered to Slack; documents via the Content Library. In build: reading email for deal context (Gmail, Outlook); summaries by email and Teams; meeting bot. Planned: CRM connection (Salesforce, HubSpot) and updates; reading deal conversations in Slack; deal status from email and Slack. Flagged: 'The CRM use cases'; 'Everything about email and Slack tracking'.
column6: Overlap: all three claim multi-channel capture. Difference: Gong frames it as multimodal signal processing; Sybill lists channels concretely. Opportunity: PitchSense's channel list matches Sybill's almost exactly — differentiation must come from how the channels are connected (memory), not the channel list itself. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): PitchSense can claim calls (transcripts) and documents today; CRM, email and Slack are In build or Planned, so the channel list is not a public claim yet.

column2: 'Know what's really happening across deals'; 'See what's happening across deals and your pipeline without asking reps' (CRO card) (https://www.sybill.ai/)
column3: 'Forecast you can stand behind. Finally.'; 'Know what's actually in your pipeline — before the board asks.' (https://www.getaida.com/solutions)
column4: 'Predict pipeline risk' (homepage, https://www.gong.io/); 'clear line of sight into your forecast, growth, and strategy execution' (https://www.gong.io/solutions/revenue-leadership)
column5: In build: deal and account pages with connected call history; deal risks (Watch / At risk); commitments tracking. Planned: agent answers about calls, deals and accounts; CRM connection. No forecasting capability at any status. Built today: list of every call, call summaries, Home, accounts and contacts created automatically.
column6: Overlap: heavy. All three own deal-visibility language. Difference: Gong predicts; Aida frames around forecast standability; Sybill emphasizes no-rep-chasing. Opportunity: the phrase space is crowded; PitchSense should avoid generic 'deal visibility' claims and tie visibility to memory-grounded evidence. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): 'Know every deal' rests on In build items; keep it out of public copy until deal pages, deal risks and commitments ship (Phase 3 Direction B).

column2: Hero mentions proposals and collateral automation; no homepage content-library or approved-content messaging (https://www.sybill.ai/)
column3: Not observed on inspected Aida pages (https://www.getaida.com/)
column4: The inspected homepage card emphasizes enablement; content-library messaging was not observed there (https://www.gong.io/)
column5: Built: Content Library with AI search and sources ('One home for approved content'); practice built from your own documents. Planned: content suggested for each call and follow-up; sales content creation (one-pagers, decks, proposals in your brand guidelines). Flagged: 'The security doc suggested from the Content Library'; 'Everything about creating one-pagers, decks and proposals'.
column6: None of the three leads homepage messaging with content intelligence. Opportunity: this is the least-contested of PitchSense's four pillars on these homepages — a potential differentiator if connected to memory (content informed by what actually happens in deals). NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): Built (Content Library with AI search and sources; practice from your own documents). 'Content informed by what happens in deals' depends on Planned per-call content suggestion.

column2: Sales-leader page: 'Build a winning team with data, not gut feeling. Ask Sybill to show you what top reps do differently across won or loss deals so you can replicate it across the team.'; homepage FAQ does not lead with coaching (https://www.sybill.ai/use-case/sales-leader)
column3: 'A coach for every rep. Not just the ones you have time for.' (https://www.getaida.com/solutions); 'Every rep gets coached on every call, with zero manager time taxed.' (https://www.getaida.com/platform)
column4: Gong Enable product card: 'Turn every rep into a top performer with the only revenue enablement solution grounded in real customer interactions.' (https://www.gong.io/); coaching signals on revenue-leadership page (https://www.gong.io/solutions/revenue-leadership)
column5: Built: AI voice roleplays (11 scenario types, 3 languages, micro roleplays); tracks; skills and scoring set by Enablement; scores with evidence on every practice session; readiness per rep and scenario; coaching suggestions for managers; one-click drills with before-and-after results. In build: pre-call drill tied to a specific upcoming call. Planned: scoring real calls on your skills. Flagged: 'Checks the score on the next real call'.
column6: Overlap: all three claim scalable coaching. Difference: Aida's coaching is per-call and in-workflow; Sybill's centers on top-performer replication and manager Q&A; Gong's is enablement-grounded ('grounded in real customer interactions'). None of the three homepages feature AI roleplay/practice prominently. Hypothesis to test: AI roleplay is homepage white space among these three — verify against roleplay specialists (Quantified, Hyperbound, Second Nature) from Phase 1 before claiming it. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): Practice, scoring with evidence and readiness are Built; coaching grounded in real calls is Planned. The roleplay-specialist check is now done: practice leads the hero of 7 of the other 40 homepages (Phase 2 synthesis; Phase 3 section 6), and Hyperbound pairs it with real-call analysis (Phase 1 update, Oct 19, 2026). Not whitespace.

column2: Ask-it-anything framing: 'Ask it anything about buyers, blockers, risks, pipeline health, coaching, or forecasting.' (https://www.sybill.ai/)
column4: Gong Agents: 'Get help with the grunt work. Discover how Gong Agents automate follow-ups, pipeline edits, enablement triggers, and forecast corrections.' (https://www.gong.io/)
column5: Built: call summaries with links to the transcript; Content Library AI search with sources; scores with evidence on every practice session; agent answers about practice, team skills and content, with sources. Planned: agent answers about calls, deals and accounts. Flagged: 'The board-meeting question to the agent'.
column6: Overlap: Q&A/ask-anything is common. Difference: none of the three foregrounds 'source-backed' or citation-grounded answers as a homepage claim. Opportunity: trust/explainability of AI answers (showing the source call/email behind every insight) is not claimed by any of the three on their homepages — a testable differentiation angle. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): Built for summaries, Content Library answers, practice scores and agent answers on practice, skills and content; Planned for answers about calls, deals and accounts. The angle is claim-safe only when scoped to Built surfaces (Phase 3 Direction A).

column2: 'Sybill automates busywork like CRM updates, email follow-ups, proposals, and collateral'; 'Save reps 10+ hours/week' (https://www.sybill.ai/)
column3: 'Aida handles the follow-up that slipped, the meeting you joined underprepared, the CRM update you forgot. You stay focused on selling.'; 'Aida auto-populates CRM fields from every call, email, and Slack message so pipeline reviews run on what actually happened.' (https://www.getaida.com/solutions)
column4: 'Automate handoffs'; 'Gong has saved us 6,700 hours across call prep, follow-up, and CRM updates' (https://www.gong.io/)
column5: Built: summaries delivered to Slack; pre-call brief in Slack 30 minutes before each meeting; accounts and contacts created automatically; Home list of what needs each rep today. In build: follow-up email drafts; agent proposals that a person approves. Planned: CRM updates; sending approved follow-up emails. Flagged: 'The CRM use cases'.
column6: Overlap: extreme — all three feature admin-reduction claims; Sybill and Gong attach quantified hours. Difference: Sybill currently makes this its primary hero (busywork/guesswork). Opportunity/avoid: generic time-savings claims are occupied (Sybill, Gong); PitchSense should avoid leading with 'save X hours' as the primary promise and instead frame admin reduction as a byproduct of memory. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): Built admin reduction is limited to Slack summaries, pre-call briefs and auto-created accounts/contacts; CRM updates are Planned, so admin reduction cannot be a lead claim.
